title: 2019 AMC 10B Problem 5
statement: Triangle \(ABC\) lies in the first quadrant. Points \(A,\) \(B,\) and \(C\) are reflected across the line \(y=x\) to points \(A',\) \(B',\) and \(C',\) respectively. Assume that none of the vertices of the triangle lie on the line \(y=x.\) Which of the following statements is not always true?

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text: Triangle \(A'B'C'\) lies in the first quadrant.

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: Triangles \(ABC\) and \(A'B'C'\) have the same area.

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: The slopes of lines \(AA'\) and \(CC'\) are the same.

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text:
Lines \(AB\) and \(A'B'\) are perpendicular to
each other.

solutions.text:
Reflection across \(y=x\) sends \((x,y)\) to \((y,x)\). It therefore preserves the first quadrant and preserves area, so A and B are always true.

The direction from \((x,y)\) to its image \((y,x)\) is \((y-x,x-y)\), whose slope is \(-1\) because \(x\ne y\). Thus C and D are always true as well.

For E, take \(A=(2,1)\), \(B=(3,2)\), and \(C=(4,1)\). These points satisfy all the conditions, but \(AB\) and \(A'B'\) both have slope \(1\), so the two lines are parallel rather than perpendicular.

Thus, the answer is E .
hints: Reflections preserve area and the first quadrant across \(y=x\)
Test the claim about \(AB\) with a simple segment of slope \(1\)
